purpose: Rank open ESS-1000 gaps for implementation and PSI idle repair without allowing score optimization to override non-compensable severity.

severity_classes.name: existential
severity_classes.meaning: active risk of unauthorized authority, data loss, unrecoverable corruption, secret exposure, tenant/project escape, safety override loss or inability to stop/restore

severity_classes.name: critical
severity_classes.meaning: correctness, authentication/authorization, privacy/deletion, supply-chain, rollback/recovery or production integrity essential is absent or regressed

severity_classes.name: high
severity_classes.meaning: reliability, testability, operability, data integrity, observability or deployment minimum blocks trustworthy operation

severity_classes.name: standard
severity_classes.meaning: required engineering/product/AI-runtime minimum remains open but does not create an immediate critical hazard

hard_order: blocked prerequisite causing broad downstream invalidation

scoring_within_same_severity.rule: Scores only order items inside the same non-compensable severity class; a lower-severity high score cannot leapfrog a higher-severity gap.

starvation.action: promote oldest eligible gap within its existing severity class

regression_policy.reason: Previously relied-upon essentials can invalidate downstream closure and therefore receive repair preference among equal-severity work.

batching.shared_dependency_conflict: serialize only conflicting mutations; unrelated lanes remain parallel

anti_gaming: severity cannot be lowered by benchmark gains
waiver cannot lower closure severity or mark complete
optional feature disablement cannot erase safe-disabled essential obligations
priority score is not completion evidence
self-improvement agents cannot rewrite severity policy during their own candidate evaluation
